meta: Buy 3 get 1 free, $12 a box, you need 10 boxes: how much do you pay? AI answers $90 right away, and it's wrong. Add just one sentence, chain of thought: "Think step by step", and AI gets $96.

muc.title: A shopping math problem
muc.text: Mark asks: buy three get one free, each box is $12, I need ten boxes, how much do I pay? AI answers right away: $90. Wrong.

muc.title: Tell AI to think step by step
muc.text: Add one sentence: think step by step. This is called chain of thought. AI writes out: two rounds of buy three get one gives eight boxes for the price of six. Two more boxes. Pay for eight boxes in total, $96.

muc.title: Writing it out gives room to think
muc.text: Because AI thinks with the very words it writes. Each step written out is more room to work things out, as in video 26 about reasoning.

muc.title: Thinking mode is built in
muc.text: Many newer models have a built-in thinking mode. With those, turning it on is enough, no extra instructions needed.

muc.title: Use it for multi-step tasks
muc.text: Use it for tasks with many steps: working out costs, comparing options, making plans. For simple things like translating one sentence, you don't need it. It just slows things down.

muc.title: Read each step to catch mistakes
muc.text: A bonus: you can read every step, so you see right away where AI went wrong, instead of just getting one number.

muc.title: Ask twice, compare
muc.text: Take a shopping math problem of your own and ask it twice, once normally and once with "think step by step" added, then compare.
